Sincerely the skills of programmers in general have gone down in the last 40 years. Programmers before had much more in depth knowledge of the actual hardware and architecture and had absolute control over the actual "metal". Today programmers are distracted by high level abstractions, and layers of frameworks, libraries, etc. that programming has turned into copy-pasting boiler plate code, and thus even a simple AI could do it. It is not "programming" anymore but truthfully it is just "configuring" a general purpose framework with "scripting". I think the software industry is going down the wrong path, and it won't end well..

Great points. AI revolution will displace and shift the job market for sure, but it's not "taking jobs". Or maybe it does... from some. From people who just got stuck on the 'button pushing', and no blaming there, if it's something you've done for a decade and now you have to do something else, it can be quite disruptive. People do tend to get into a 'flow'. But globally, AI does not make people obsolete. It just shift perspective onto a higher level. For programmers it means - more work done, more programs, more features, more polish, more things automated. And slop? Sure. But it's not AI's fault. We had sloppy software before. It was just a lot less of it. Now we'll get more software in general, and naturally we'll get more slop. But also more gems. And same with everything. You can already see it. Have anyone noticed a sudden surge in lots of small quality of life and UI\UX improvements in softwares that existed for years already? Like... idk... todoist? Like advanced skeleton for maya - the website, the plugin itself. A lot of the small-priority but important bug fixes, improvements, style reworks were delayed for years because they were just not important enough to dedicate human hours to them. Now? You can just let AI do that.
